hints.title: The Core Recognition Clue
hints.text: Notice the word 'strictly increasing'. Can you ever loop back to a cell you already visited? No! Because every step strictly increases the cell value. That means this matrix is an IMPLICIT Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with M * N nodes.

hints.title: Subproblem & State Formulation
hints.text: Define dfs(r, c) = the length of the longest increasing path starting at cell (r, c). Because there are no cycles, the subproblem depends ONLY on cells with strictly larger values.

hints.title: Transition Recurrence
hints.text: For cell (r, c), check all 4 neighbors (nr, nc). If matrix[nr][nc] > matrix[r][c], path length is 1 + dfs(nr, nc). If no neighbor is larger, the base case is 1. Memoize this: dp[r][c] = 1 + max([0] + [dfs(nr, nc) for valid neighbors]).
